label: Florida: sale duties without the billion-dollar gate
note: Verified editorial summary, not a verbatim statutory extract. Primary text retrieved for the September 22, 2026 applicability candidate. A narrow surviving-duty screen; exemptions in the linked chapter still require their own analysis.
body: A person meeting §501.702(9)(a)1–3 must not sell sensitive personal data without prior consumer consent; this provision does not require the billion-dollar or specified business-model criteria.

The section prescribes a sensitive-data sale notice. If the sensitive data belongs to a known child, it requires affirmative authorization for a child between13 and18, or COPPA compliance for a known child under13. Check age, knowledge and the precise statutory sensitive-data definition.
